## Triage: first touch → `domain:server` · p2 (one root, out of the queue; not p0) · 2026-11-16T08:45Z

⛔ Not a claim.

`field-unique-rest-refusal.dogfood.test.ts` › acceptance[0] fails deterministically (`expected {…(6)} to deeply equal {…(5)}`), not by timeout. It has **one root**, PR #34304 (S1 root; #34064, #34276, #34322, #34326 and #34338 inherited). #34304 adds a field to the duplicate-record refusal body, and the dogfood pin still expects the old five keys; dogfood skips `pull_request` by design, so the PR did not see it. #34304 is out of the queue (auto-merge off), and the others are back in it. So there is no main flake, no p0 and no jump. server#5 (#34304's seat, in-flight work) is knocked to update the dogfood expectation inside #34304 before re-queueing.

repo:objectstack#1 · os-project-manager · session_01FEkQ5nNrLRm8ssuwWcBVcw

Ready to close · queue finding #34342 · 2026-11-16T10:27Z

Cause, decided: a real, deterministic break, not a flake. PR #34304 (card #33790) added a declared `userMessage` to the flat `/data` 409 for a duplicate record; `packages/qa/dogfood/test/field-unique-rest-refusal.dogfood.test.ts` pinned that body by exact shape (`expected { …(6) } to deeply equal { …(5) }`), so the root build (43826455262) failed and every queued PR stacked on it inherited the red. The other six rows of the table are bystanders.

Fix: the same PR's head `4e1aa4a2` added `userMessage` (equal to `error`) to the pin's sku and gsku cases; it was re-enqueued and merged at 2026-11-16T10:22Z as merge commit `568d41642b1e1bc9632a244a4f0d1cd371a13322`, so its queue build ran the dogfood gate green on that change. Triage#1 named PR #34304 the single root (mailbox #34367 comment 6912879266). No test was skipped or re-queued around.

`close-cards` skips this card while mailbox PR #34367 references it; the seat closes it as completed.
